ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024); Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (effective 1 January 2020); Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended and currently in force); PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 - Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Ownership Information (effective 1 November 2024); Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration; and relevant SAMR/PBOC implementing rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the document is issued in a Hague Apostille Convention State: notarize/certify in the country of origin, obtain an Apostille from the competent authority, then produce a certified Simplified Chinese translation; do NOT add consular legalization. If issued in a non-member state: notarize/certify, authenticate through the origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs, obtain consular legalization from the PRC Embassy/Consulate, then produce a certified Simplified Chinese translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incumbency
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or registered agent of the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same parallel path as Certificate of Incorporation: Apostille for Hague member states; consular legalization for non-member states. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and/or Power of Attorney appointing the WFOE legal representative, directors, and supervisor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signatures must be notarized in origin; then apply either Apostille (Hague member) or consular legalization (non-member). Include certified Simplified Chinese translation. Apostille path and consular path are alternatives, not cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and Articles of the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or legal representative of the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy must be notarized in origin; then either Apostille by competent authority (Hague member) or consular legalization by PRC Embassy/Consulate after foreign ministry authentication (non-member). Never chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent or relationship bank of the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter must be signed by bank officer and notarized or legalized per destination bank requirements. If used for AML/KYC file in China, it normally does not require Apostille/consular legalization, but if required by the Chinese bank, apply either Apostille or consular legalization according to origin state; choose one path only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Register Extract or Ownership Structure Chart of the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of beneficial ownership or corporate secretary / legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Where issued by a public registry, use Apostille for Hague member states and consular legalization for non-members. Where issued privately by legal counsel, notarization plus the appropriate single-choice authentication path is acceptable for SAMR/PBOC UBO filing.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be completed for every ultimate beneficial owner, director, legal representative, supervisor, senior manager, authorized signatory, material counterparty, and bank account signatory. Screening sources include the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, EU/UK financial sanctions lists if relevant, PRC public security and terrorist list, PBOC adverse financial-integrity data, court enforcement and credit blacklists, and domestic regulator-disqualified person registers. PEP status must be checked against politically exposed person databases, including domestic and foreign PEP lists, immediate family, and close associates. The AML risk tier for this low-risk B2B marketplace remains Low_Risk_Standard, but enhanced due diligence applies whenever the counterparty is a PEP, high-risk jurisdiction, or sanctioned vessel/entity, and all negative hits must be escalated to the AML compliance officer before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) through the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); name pre-reservation is processed on the provincial SAMR online service platform under the Enterprise Registration and Name Reservation module.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal registered name of a WFOE must be expressed in Simplified Chinese logographs only; traditional Chinese or foreign script is not accepted as the statutory name. The name must follow the four-tier statutory structure: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry or business characteristics + organizational form. The foreign investor may use a pinyin transliteration or English trade name in bank instructions and company seals, but such transliteration does not replace the Simplified Chinese registered name. All submitted translations of foreign documents must be in Simplified Chinese, and the registered name must not contain numerals, misleading superlatives, or conflicting industry descriptors unless duly approved.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name reservation is rejected, the applicant must first read the SAMR rejection reason and correct the prohibited token or structural conflict. The applicant may file a written administrative reconsideration application with the market regulation authority at the next higher level within 60 days of the rejection notice, or directly file an administrative lawsuit with the competent people's court within 6 months. The appeal brief must explain the exact expected name, proposed alternative names, evidence of prior ministerial approval for any sensitive token, and legal grounds under the Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A shell virtual office or commercial mailbox-only address is not permissible for a WFOE in mainland China. SAMR requires a definite, verifiable registered address within the administrative district, and the tax authority requires an actual place and effective business contact for invoice issuance, payroll, social insurance, and inspection. A shared-service or clustered registered address may be accepted in some free-trade zones and approved incubation zones, but the company must still maintain physical staff, business records, and communications at that address or a declared operational subsidiary site. For this B2B cross-border e-commerce platform, payment banks and Alipay/Pay-related onboarding will reject a mailbox-only address; at minimum a rent-backed office or licensed co-working space with lease agreements, utility invoices, and local management access is required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) address matches lease and property tax bill; (2) company nameplate is displayed; (3) authorized employee/legal representative is present; (4) original lease, VAT invoices for rent, utility bills, and employee payroll records are accessible; (5) business equipment and server/communication infrastructure are on-site. Quantified risk: a genuine physical office with full records carries a Low unannounced-inspection probability of 5-10% per year; a clustered/hosted free-trade-zone address with adequate substance carries 15-30% probability; a premises mismatch or mailbox-type address carries 50-80% probability and will trigger immediate verification, incapability-to-operate findings, and possible revocation of registration.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Origin notary public, origin foreign ministry or Apostille authority, PRC Embassy/Consulate, and certified translation agency
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular and notarial tariff plus prevailing market rate per translated page and per document set.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of Good Standing issued by the foreign investor home registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official certificate fee as published by the registry, plus courier and expediting charges if required.
Bank service tariff for corporate reference letters; may be waived at relationship manager's discretion.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PRC corporate legal drafting and compliance review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market hourly rate for drafting Articles of Association, corporate governance records, UBO filing checklist, and employment/rental agreements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company seal engraving and public-security filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Provincial or municipal public security price guideline for statutory Chinese-language company seals.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO information collection, verification, and PBOC/SAMR filing support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance service provider or PRC law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market compliance service fee; no PBOC/SAMR official filing fee is charged for UBO record submission.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 4, 8, 10, 13, 16, 20, 24, 28, 30, 32, 33, 35, 50 and 51; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020), Articles 4, 12, 14, 26 and 28; Regulation on the Implementation of the Foreign Investment Law (State Council Order No. 723), Articles 7, 14 and 24.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Enterprise Registration Division of the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) under the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) in the jurisdiction where the registered office is located.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Foreign-Invested Company together with the adopted Articles of Association, as accepted by the AMR and evidenced by issuance of the Business License.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise under current Chinese law. The registered capital amount, currency and contribution schedule are set by the shareholders in the Articles of Association and must be reasonably consistent with the business scope. There is no blocked escrow account requirement. The declared capital must be actually paid under the agreed schedule and the amount may not be removed or withdrawn except under lawful capital reduction or dissolution procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED, A WHOLLY FOREIGN-OWNED ENTERPRISE, adopted on ________ at ________. WHEREAS the sole shareholder has executed the Articles of Association and all necessary incorporation instruments; and WHEREAS the directors have been duly appointed and have accepted office; and WHEREAS these resolutions are adopted to organize the company in accordance with the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Foreign Investment Law. NOW THEREFORE, the board of directors resolves unanimously as follows: 1. Share Capital Subscription. The board acknowledges receipt of the capital contribution schedules and confirms that the registered capital of the company is [amount] represented by [number] issued and fully subscribed shares, contributed by the shareholder in cash or in kind as disclosed in the Articles of Association. The board records that the subscribed capital must be paid no later than the statutory contribution deadline and shall not be withdrawn except as permitted by law. 2. Banking Authorization. The board authorizes [legal representative] and [general manager] to open, manage and close corporate bank accounts with licensed commercial banks in China; to execute account applications, delegation of authority, online banking contracts and remittance instructions; and to designate at least two authorized signatories for all payment and settlement transactions, subject to the corporate financial controls. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office of the company is fixed at [registered address], China, and the board authorizes the legal representative to execute lease or service agreements, make address filings, and receive service of process at that address. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. Effective immediately, [name] is appointed executive director and legal representative; [name] is appointed as supervisor; [name] is appointed general manager; [name] is appointed chief financial officer; and [name] is appointed compliance officer. Each officer shall act within the scope of authority granted by the Articles of Association and shall hold office until removed. 5. Delegation and Ratification. The legal representative and general manager are jointly and severally authorized to prepare, execute, notarize and file all documents, contracts, and applications required by the Administration for Market Regulation, the tax authority, the bank and any other government department; and all acts previously performed by the promoters, counsel and proposed officers in connection with the formation are hereby ratified, confirmed and approved in all respects. This resolution is irrevocable, effective upon adoption, and a copy shall be delivered to the company's statutory records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-registration enterprise name reservation and Foreign Investment Negative List screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) through the name reservation module of the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform (Yiwangtongban); the State Administration for Market Regulation reviews any name containing the words China or National.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed enterprise name through the corporate name reservation module of the local Administration for Market Regulation using the national integrated online government service platform. The name must follow the prescribed order: administrative division, company name, industry descriptor, and company type suffix. The platform will conduct an automated and manual conflict check against the national enterprise name database. For a WFOE, the applicant must simultaneously confirm that the planned business scope does not fall into the prohibited category of the Foreign Investment Negative List. Submit three alternative names, verify the legal representative's identity, and obtain the electronic Name Reservation Notice before proceeding to the establishment filing.
required_dossiers: Completed enterprise name reservation application form
Passport or identity document of the proposed legal representative
Projected business scope and investment structure description
Certificate of the foreign investor and chain of ownership
Power of attorney and agent identity if submitted through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected for conflict or prohibited characters, the applicant shall submit a revised name reservation with the alternative names within two working days. If the business scope touches a restricted sector in the Foreign Investment Negative List, the proposed scope shall be narrowed or the applicant shall submit the sector-specific licence or administration agreement before the establishment filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Domicile procurement, Articles of Association drafting and foreign document authentication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR), assisted by a licenced notary office or commercial counsel; overseas documents shall be notarized, legalized or apostilled and accompanied by certified Chinese translation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure a lawful registered address before submitting the incorporation application. The address must correspond to a physical premise acceptable to the local AMR under the applicable residential or commercial address regulations. After executing the lease agreement and landlord consent, the foreign investor or its representative shall prepare the Articles of Association in Chinese, stating the company name, address, business scope, registered capital, capital contribution schedule, governance structure, legal representative clause, supervisor appointment, and liquidation provisions. If the investor is an overseas company, the investor's certificate of good standing and identity documents must be notarized and apostilled or legalized for PRC use, then translated into Chinese by a certified translation agency.
required_dossiers: Business lease agreement or office service agreement for the registered address
Property ownership certificate of the landlord or the landlord's certificate of title
Identity document or certificate of the landlord and the consent to use the premises
Draft Articles of Association in Chinese signed by the shareholder or authorized representative
Notarized and apostilled or legalized certificate of incorporation and good standing of the foreign investor
Certified Chinese translation of the foreign investor documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AMR queries the domicile, the applicant shall provide a written domicile compliance statement issued by the landlord or the local neighborhood committee. If the lease is deemed temporary or non-compliant, the company shall replace the address or obtain an extension of the landlord consent and refile before the establishment application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of establishment registration application and foreign investment information filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) one-stop service window; the foreign investment information report is filed through the integrated commerce department platform collected by the AMR registration system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete establishment registration application through the local AMR one-stop service window. Submit the application form signed by the legal representative, the original Name Reservation Notice, the executed Articles of Association, appointment documents for the executive director, legal representative, supervisor, and general manager, proof of registered address, and a capital contribution certificate or a written commitment letter. The AMR will review the application under the Company Law and issue the Business License with a Uniform Social Credit Code. After the license is issued, the foreign investment information report must be filed with the competent commerce department through the integrated online platform unless the registry has already collected it.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Foreign-Invested Company signed by the legal representative
Online or printed Name Reservation Notice
Original executed Articles of Association
Appointment and identity documents of executive director, legal representative, supervisor, general manager and compliance officer
Proof of registered address and lease
Capital contribution schedule or written commitment letter
Foreign Investment Negative List compliance statement
Foreign investment information reporting form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AMR issues a notice of supplementary correction, all missing documents and explanations shall be submitted through the online system within five working days. If the application is suspended for negative list concerns, the applicant shall provide the sector-specific license or amend the business scope. If the foreign investment report is rejected, the company shall correct the investment details and resubmit through the integrated platform within ten days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate seal filing and bank account activation with post-registration governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau authorized seal engraving agency; licensed commercial bank in China; local tax and social insurance authorities for follow-on registrations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Business License is issued, apply to a Public Security Bureau-authorized seal engraving company for the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, contract seal, and legal representative seal. The legal representative or an authorized officer must carry the license and the seal engraving permit to the bank to open the basic deposit account. The bank will conduct AML/KYC verification and may request corporate governance documents. The account mandate must identify at least two signatories, one of whom shall be the legal representative or authorized financial officer. After the account is activated, the company must register for tax, social insurance, housing fund and, if applicable, foreign exchange management using the Uniform Social Credit Code as the taxpayer identifier.
required_dossiers: Original Business License and Uniform Social Credit Code certificate
Seal engraving permit from the public security administrative authorization
Legal representative passport or resident identity document
First board resolution appointing bank signatories and the financial control policy
Office lease contract or service address proof
Articles of Association and register of members
Tax registration form and social insurance registration information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional KYC disclosure, the company shall provide source of funds declarations, detailed business plan and a beneficial ownership chart. If the seal engraving permit is revoked or rejected because of missing signatures, the legal representative shall submit a written authorization and the corrected appointment resolution to the authorized engraving office and reapply within three working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration, invoicing setup and post-formation licence applicability confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local office of the State Taxation Administration, National Bureau of Statistics, and State Administration of Foreign Exchange if cross-border payments are anticipated.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the tax registration using the Uniform Social Credit Code as the taxpayer identification number, and register for corporate income tax, value-added tax, and relevant surtaxes. Apply for electronic invoice quotas and digital tax control equipment activation through the provincial electronic tax bureau service portal. Confirm whether the B2B cross-border marketplace activity requires export/import customs registration or foreign exchange settlement filings under the applicable State Administration of Foreign Exchange regulations. Prepare a written operational assessment confirming that ISIC 4791 is a digital intermediary activity and that no industrial, EIA or civil defense operating licences are required at the registered administrative office. Retain the assessment in the statutory records for regulatory audits.
required_dossiers: Business License with Uniform Social Credit Code
Articles of Association and first board resolution
Bank basic deposit account opening certificate and account mandate
Identity document of legal representative and financial officer
Seal registration certificate or company seal specimen
Initial tax registration information form including expected turnover and business scope
Foreign exchange registration form if outbound remittance or collection in foreign currency is expected
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority queries the business scope or expected turnover, the company shall submit a written explanation supported by the platform contracts and a financial projection. If the electronic invoice quota is insufficient, the company may request a temporary quota increase by filing the business forecast and tax compliance certificate. Any potential customs registration issue shall be cured by filing a customs declaration unit registration with the local customs authority before the first cross-border shipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. The registered scope, ISIC 4791 Electronic B2B Wholesale Platform Operation, is a non-manufacturing, non-chemical, non-assembly and non-warehousing digital activity. No industrial licensing authority is triggered. If the company later adds physical operations, the local Administration for Market Regulation, Emergency Management Bureau and Ecology and Environment Bureau will become the competent authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. There is no mandatory industrial operating licence under China's Catalogue of Administrative Licensing Items for this platform model. Any future commercial activity requiring a value-added telecommunications permit is outside the industrial licensing assessment and would be evaluated under telecommunications regulations, not this industrial licensing docket.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China through the local Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable and Exempt. The digital B2B marketplace does not involve construction, production, or pollutant discharge, and therefore does not trigger an Environmental Impact Assessment Report, Environmental Impact Registration, or acceptance under the Classified Management List for Environmental Impact Assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. No wastewater, volatile organic compounds, or hazardous waste streams are generated by the platform operation. If a future warehousing or fulfillment facility is established, wastewater discharge shall comply with Integrated Wastewater Discharge Standard GB 8978, volatile organic compounds shall comply with Emission Standard of Air Pollutants for Volatile Organic Compounds GB 37822, and hazardous wastes shall be managed under the Law on Prevention and Control of Environmental Pollution by Solid Waste.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable. There is no physical premises requiring a Civil Defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or workplace safety pre-evaluation under the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China. Standard office workplace safety rules remain applicable. If a physical fulfillment site is established in the future, the company must obtain a fire safety design review, fire safety acceptance inspection, and occupational safety pre-evaluation before operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) via the Electronic Tax Bureau (电子税务局) portal at https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity establishing a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) must first complete commercial incorporation with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), which issues a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) that serves as the taxpayer identification number (TIN). Within 30 days of obtaining the business license, the WFOE must complete supplementary tax registration at the competent local tax authority through the Electronic Tax Bureau, binding the USCC to tax filings. The applicant must submit the business license, articles of association, legal representative identification, and proof of registered address. Upon activation, the taxpayer obtains an electronic tax account, VAT taxpayer qualification (general or small-scale taxpayer), and the right to issue electronic invoices through the STA-approved digital invoice system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box entity classification election exists under Chinese income tax law. However, a WFOE may elect simplified small-scale taxpayer VAT treatment if annual taxable sales are below 5,000,000 CNY, or may voluntarily register as a general VAT taxpayer subject to conditions. No hybrid mismatch elections are available under domestic Chinese tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 5,000,000 CNY annual aggregate taxable sales for mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration; entities below this threshold remain registered as small-scale taxpayers and are subject to simplified collection rates.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates full digitalized electronic invoicing for registered enterprises under the Shanghai and nationwide Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice (全电发票) reform. Taxpayers must integrate business systems with the STA e-invoice platform via API or web-based services for real-time issuance, transmission, and archiving. The Golden Tax System IV (金税四期) performs central real-time verification of invoice data, transaction matching, and anti-fraud risk analytics. Issuance is not subject to pre-printing fiscal clearance, but all invoice data must synchronize with the STA within the statutory reporting cycle; non-compliance triggers automated blocking of issuance rights.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for goods applies when the WFOE exports physical goods from China customs territory under an export sales contract, completes the electronic customs export declaration (报关单), and obtains customs release records. For services, zero-rated cross-border supply applies to services sold to non-resident recipients where the services are rendered entirely outside China or where the recipient uses them outside China; B2B marketplace facilitation services satisfying these conditions qualify. The taxpayer must claim the zero rate on the VAT return, file an export tax refund declaration, and retain complete supporting documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (报关单) with electronic release message
Bill of Lading (sea) or Airway Bill (air) issued by a licensed carrier
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Receipt Voucher (出口收汇核销单) or bank statement evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Export sales contract or purchase order with the offshore buyer
Special VAT invoice for export (if issued under the export taxation rules)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and General Administration of Customs may jointly audit export zero-rating claims for up to five or more years retrospectively. Any unsubstantiated, fraudulent, or non-repatriated export transaction triggers recovery of the refunded VAT amount, late payment surcharge, and monetary penalties ranging from 50% to five times the refunded sum under the Tax Administration Law. Failure to repatriate foreign exchange within 180 days may invalidate the zero-rating and lead to clawback, customs fines, downgrade of customs credit rating, suspension of export tax refund qualification, and potential criminal liability for fraudulent refunds under Chinese Criminal Law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) as the central bank, with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) as the delegated foreign exchange control regulator and licensing authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains current-account convertibility for trade and services, allowing WFOE treasury operations to buy and sell foreign currency through designated banks at market rates once the underlying transaction is verified. The capital account, however, remains strictly controlled and requires ex ante SAFE or bank-delegated registration for inbound FDI, offshore lending, and foreign-currency loans. Export proceeds are repatriated and can be retained in a foreign-exchange account or settled into RMB without a forced conversion ratio, but banks must electronically match the funds against customs declarations and commercial invoices. Profit remittance by a WFOE is treated as current-account income only after tax: the bank must see an audited statutory financial statement, corporate profit distribution resolution, tax clearance certificate, and a statutory audit opinion confirming realized profits. Once converted capital is in RMB, the WFOE cannot invest it in entrusted loans, securities, or non-operating real estate unless specifically permitted; every cross-border flow must be tagged with a valid purpose code and reconciled with the enterprise's actual business scope. For a B2B marketplace, receipts from overseas merchants require careful segregation between the platform's own settlement income and agency collection flows to avoid AML layering concerns.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign-currency receipts must be repatriated to Mainland China and registered through the bank's trade monitoring system; the standard verification and surrender window is 180 days from collection or customs declaration. The mandatory conversion ratio is zero, so a WFOE may retain 100 percent of verified export proceeds in a domestic foreign-exchange account or sell them to a designated bank for RMB at market rates, subject to proof of actual trade background and customs data matching.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Cross-Border Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Not viable for domestic Mainland treasury. A WFOE cannot rely on offshore fintech EMIs such as Revolut, Wise Business, or Airwallex as its primary clearing bank because they lack PBOC/SAFE licenses to open RMB or foreign-currency settlement accounts inside China and are legally barred from being the direct banking interface for a PRC entity. Such EMIs may only support the offshore parent side of the structure, routing verified capital into China through a licensed bank; they cannot clear Alipay-settled marketplace proceeds or execute SAFE-regulated FX transactions on behalf of the WFOE. The sole compliant structure is a wholly domestic tier-1 commercial bank account, complemented by the platform's payment institution license.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The legal representative and at least one authorized financial signatory must complete an in-branch or PBOC-compliant high-definition video interview with the domestic bank; a pure remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted for the basic settlement and foreign-exchange accounts. A foreign legal representative may grant a notarized and legalized power of attorney to a local resident officer for document filing, but the representative's identity, signature, and source of funds must still be verified through a direct interview or recognized digital KYC session approved by the bank's compliance committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered ownership chain where the Chinese WFOE sits beneath offshore intermediate holding companies, making the ultimate beneficial owner difficult to identify.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and legalized corporate charters, certificate of incumbency, and register of members for every entity in the ownership chain from the WFOE up to each individual; shareholder registers and capital logs showing all intermediate transfers; passport copies and sanctions/PEP screening results for every natural person holding at least 25 percent of the structure; source-of-wealth declaration supported by investment agreements or dividend records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial FDI capital injection funded by a low-tax jurisdiction parent with limited operating history or no obvious commercial rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original FDI contract and irrevocable board resolution; three years of audited financial statements for the remitting parent; 12 months of bank statements for the remitting account; formal bank reference letter from the remitting institution; legal opinion confirming economic substance and absence of shell status; detailed business plan and projected cash-flow model for the B2B marketplace platform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction pattern mismatch where the B2B marketplace receives numerous small cross-border payments through third-party payment institutions, allowing the appearance of deposit-taking or layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of platform settlement reports showing merchant identifiers and transaction IDs; executed master service agreements with merchants and suppliers; payment gateway and Alibaba Pay integration agreements; AML and KYC policies applied to onboarded merchants; reconciliation between platform ledgers, payment institution statements, and the WFOE bank account; enterprise income tax and VAT filings corresponding to the declared revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed person or unexplained wealth identified behind the legal representative or ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed PEP questionnaire and AML declaration for all directors, shareholders, and signatories; notarized identification documents and residential address proof; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth report based on salary, dividends, or real-asset liquidation; personal tax returns and independent wealth evidence; negative media search reports from at least two professional screening databases; written undertaking to maintain enhanced ongoing monitoring.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The offshore parent must wire the FDI capital contribution by SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's designated foreign-exchange capital account at a licensed PRC bank. The remittance message must carry the SAFE-recognized purpose code for inbound direct investment capital contribution and reference the FDI registration or Foreign Investment Basic Information Report filed for the entity. The receiving bank verifies the capital against the business license capital scope, board resolution, and FDI file, then records the flow in SAFE's cross-border foreign-currency reporting system. Capital held in the escrow capital account is quarantined until a licensed PRC certified public accountant issues a capital verification opinion confirming the injection has been received and booked; only then may the foreign currency be settled into RMB or used for approved operating needs. Settlement to the RMB basic account must preserve the audit trail of the original purpose code and is not available for entrusted loans, equity investment, securities transactions, or loans to non-affiliated third parties.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For supplier payments and paid-out merchant balances under the B2B marketplace, banks process SWIFT MT103 messages for low-value current-account payments, commercial letters of credit for high-value physical goods, and documentary collections when documents are time-staged. Every outbound remittance must be preceded by the underlying trade contract, customs declaration where goods move cross-border, tax invoices, and a SAFE-compliant purpose code. RMB cross-border flows may clear through CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System) or the applicable RTGS rail, while foreign-currency flows clear through SWIFT correspondent banking. The bank's trade finance desk will match each disbursement against the merchant reconciliation record and platform agreement to prevent phantom trade.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/FX forward contracts executed through a licensed domestic bank with documented current-account exposure and SAFE real-demand verification
Onshore FX swaps between RMB and foreign currencies for tenor-matched conversion of operational cash flows
Onshore cross-currency interest-rate swaps to hedge cross-currency borrowing or long-term investment obligations
Plain-vanilla FX options (call and put) with notional directly tied to forecast B2B marketplace receipts and supplier payments
Offshore RMB nondeliverable forwards are not permitted as hedging tools for a Mainland entity; onshore hedges must remain deliverable and covered by genuine commercial risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Report (annual business license publicity filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January through 30 June of each following calendar year; the reporting year is the immediately preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inclusion in the Abnormal Operations Directory; if not remedied within three consecutive years, inclusion in the Serious Illegal and Dishonest Enterprise List with joint government disciplinary restrictions; a company that remains non-operational or unreachable may face administrative revocation/deregistration by the registration authority

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Information Annual Report (foreign investor and WFOE investment information return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and SAMR integrated annual reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January through 30 June of each following calendar year for the prior year's foreign investment information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Order to rectify within 20 days; failure to rectify attracts a fine of CNY 100,000 to CNY 300,000 (approximately USD 14,000 to USD 42,000), increased up to CNY 500,000 in serious cases; repeated non-compliance is recorded in the public credit system and can contribute to administrative revocation proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement and Reconciliation Return (annual CIT settlement filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (SAT) through the competent local tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January through 31 May of each year following the tax year; quarterly prepayments remain separately due within 15 days after each quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of up to CNY 2,000, or CNY 2,000 to CNY 10,000 in serious cases; late-paid tax bears a surcharge of 0.05% per day from the statutory due date; evasion or false declaration may trigger penalties of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax and criminal liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual FDI Stock Equity Declaration (foreign direct investment equity information return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the designated bank or SAFE online system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January through 30 June for the previous calendar year's foreign investment stock equity position
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The entity is placed on the SAFE foreign exchange abnormal/inspection list and its capital-account foreign exchange business is suspended until the report is filed; administrative fines of up to CNY 30,000 may be imposed; prolonged non-compliance blocks profit remittance and capital-account transactions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Information Confirmation and Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR Beneficial Owner Information Registry administered with the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually confirmed through the Annual Enterprise Information Report by 30 June; any shareholding or beneficial-owner change must be reported within 30 calendar days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Correction orders and fines of up to CNY 50,000 (approximately USD 7,000) for failure to file or update beneficial owner information; incorrect or stale UBO filings are recorded in the enterprise credit system and may block equity transfer approvals and public filing clearances

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: China imposes a universal audit mandate under the PRC Company Law: every limited liability company, including a WFOE, must have its annual financial statements audited by an independent licensed CPA firm. There are no balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount exemption thresholds for ordinary WFOEs; the audit obligation is triggered by simple status as a company. Financial institutions, listed issuers, and platform companies designated by regulators may be subject to additional asset, transaction-volume, or risk-based audit and assurance requirements, but the baseline is non-quantitative and mandatory for all companies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE / China GAAP), substantially converged with IFRS; qualifying small-scale enterprises may apply the simplified ASBE for Small Enterprises, although WFOEs with cross-border activities generally apply full ASBE; statutory accounts must be prepared in RMB and in the Chinese language basis for legal records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under China's Beneficial Owner Information Management Measures, a WFOE must identify and record its beneficial owners, file the initial UBO information with SAMR, confirm and update that information through the annual enterprise report each year by 30 June, and file any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership within 30 calendar days of the change. Share transfers themselves must be reflected in the register of shareholders and submitted to SAMR as an equity-change registration within 30 days; stamped board/shareholder resolutions and the amended articles of association must accompany the filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Senior Officers
Register of Charges / Security Interests over Company Assets
Statutory Minute Book (shareholders and board meetings)
Register of Company Seals and Chops
Financial and accounting books, vouchers, and annual audit reports

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 to USD 3,000 per annum for a compliant registered-address or agency maintenance service; substantially higher for a physical leased registered office in tier-1 cities, where annual rent and ancillary administrative support commonly range from USD 10,000 to USD 100,000
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 to USD 12,000 per annum for a typical WFOE audit performed by a licensed Chinese CPA firm, depending on transaction volume, balance-sheet complexity, and the B2B marketplace platform's cross-border payment flows

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified High/New Technology Enterprises may apply a reduced 15% rate where the B2B platform owns qualifying intellectual property and satisfies R&D intensity, revenue, and technology thresholds; qualifying small low-profit enterprises benefit from an effective 5% rate on taxable income up to RMB 3 million under the 2023-2027 extension; qualifying R&D expenses may be claimed at a 100% additional deduction (total 200% deduction); no general patent-box regime exists, and no automatic free-zone tax holiday applies to an ordinary WFOE, although Hainan Free Trade Port or certain encouraged-industry zones can provide a 15% preferential rate if the platform business qualifies and meets the 60% encouraged-industry gross-income test.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form A Class) - Main Form A100000 together with the full schedule package, filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing system (eTax); quarterly provisional payments are made on Form A200000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional CIT returns and payments are due within 15 days after each calendar quarter-end; the final annual CIT return, supporting schedules, and any balance payment are due no later than 31 May of the following year; annual tax settlement must reconcile the four provisional payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter gross operating income from B2B marketplace activities, including commission fees, subscription fees, platform promotional service fees, payment facilitation fees, and value-added seller services, reconciled with PRC accounting standards and VAT returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All operating revenue earned by the Chinese WFOE is taxable in China on a worldwide basis. Do not unilaterally net out foreign taxes or treaty deductions from gross revenue. If the platform receives payments from non-resident buyers or sellers, the amount must still be fully reported; any foreign income tax paid may be claimed only through the foreign tax credit schedule. If revenue is artificially diverted to a foreign affiliate, the tax authority will recharacterize the arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter direct costs of providing platform services, including cloud hosting, bandwidth, data-center charges, payment gateway fees, software amortization, seller support, and direct labor of platform operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments to non-resident service providers must be tested for Chinese withholding obligations. A deduction is denied if the foreign provider earns income through a Chinese service PE without registration and tax filing. Related-party service costs must satisfy the actual-service, arm's-length, and benefit tests; a mere invoice from an offshore affiliate without substance is not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharge, stamp duty, property tax, land use tax, and other deductible taxes attributable to the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Value-added tax, customs duties, and VAT withheld on behalf of non-resident sellers are not CIT-deductible. If the WFOE merely facilitates transactions between non-resident sellers and Chinese buyers, taxable profit is the net commission rather than gross settlement; do not treat circular cross-border VAT flows as tax expense.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter marketing, advertising, seller acquisition, platform promotion, business development, and logistics-related selling expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If advertising or traffic acquisition is purchased from a foreign related party, the WFOE must demonstrate that the service was actually performed, produced economic benefit, and was not a disguised profit distribution. The payer must withhold income tax and VAT on taxable services sourced in China unless domestic withholding or treaty exemption applies; failure to do so triggers withholding-agent penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter headquarters overhead, rental, professional fees, salaries, depreciation, and ordinary administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees and intercompany charges from a foreign parent are deductible only with contracts, invoices, functional evidence, and an arm's-length fee. Fees that merely represent a share of profits or duplicate costs already borne by the Chinese entity are non-deductible. The annual related-party disclosure schedule must identify every cross-border administrative and service payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter interest expense, financing fees, bank charges, exchange losses, and other finance costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to foreign related parties is limited by the PRC thin-capitalization rules (debt-to-equity limit of 2:1 generally, 5:1 for financial enterprises). Interest paid to non-resident lenders without a PE is subject to 10% non-resident withholding tax unless a treaty reduces the rate. The WFOE must file the withholding return and obtain the lender's Tax Residency Certificate before applying any treaty-reduced rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter impairment losses on trade receivables, loans, goodwill, and long-lived assets recognized under Chinese accounting standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Impairment deductions require objective evidence and a recognized accounting policy. Intercompany receivables from offshore group entities must be actively managed and collected; a non-collectible receivable from a foreign shell affiliate may be challenged as a constructive dividend or deductible expense recharacterization, generating WHT and CIT exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter fair-value gains or losses on financial instruments and other measurement items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE holds derivatives, loans, or equity interest in offshore vehicles, the tax authority may attribute income to China if the assets are managed and controlled from China. Fair-value gains on cross-border related-party financial assets must be reported transparently and supported by valuation documents acceptable to the local tax bureau.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute operating profit as revenue less cost of operations, taxes and surcharges, selling expenses, administrative expenses, financial expenses, asset impairment losses, and fair-value changes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This accounting profit is the starting point for the annual CIT reconciliation. Cross-border adjustments such as transfer-pricing increases, thin-capitalization add-backs, non-deductible management fees, and denial of improperly claimed treaty benefits are made on the reconciliation schedules and carried into taxable income; they must never be embedded in accounting books.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter profit before income tax after adding non-operating income and deducting non-operating expenses on the main return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source income of the WFOE is taxable in China with a foreign tax credit. Dividends received from foreign subsidiaries are not automatically participation-exempt; calculate the foreign tax credit carefully. Dividends paid by the WFOE to its non-resident shareholder must not be deducted anywhere on this return; they are subject to separate dividend WHT at source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter taxable income after application of tax-exempt income, non-taxable income, deductible items, loss carryforwards, and special tax adjustments in the corresponding schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a transfer pricing adjustment or GAAR recharacterization is imposed, the increased taxable income is reflected here. The WFOE must maintain the full transfer-pricing documentation, functional analysis, and economic substance evidence for at least ten years. Any net operating loss used from prior years must comply with the five-year carryforward limit unless a special high-tech loss extension applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the final annual CIT liability by applying the statutory or preferential rate to taxable income and offsetting quarterly prepayments and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a WFOE, the CIT liability is borne by the Chinese entity itself. The non-resident parent shareholder does not file CIT through this return; instead, any dividend, interest, royalty, or service payment to the parent is subjected to non-resident withholding at 10% statutory rates or reduced treaty rates upon proper application. The WFOE must file the withholding return through the e-tax system and remit WHT separately before the remittance leaves China.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return or schedules can attract a fixed penalty of RMB 2,000, rising to RMB 2,000-10,000 for serious cases under PRC Tax Collection Administration Law Article 62. Late payment of CIT accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% on unpaid tax until payment. Understatement or false declaration of taxable income is treated as tax evasion under Article 63, with fines of 50 percent to five times the underpaid tax plus full collection of tax and interest. Fraudulent tax evasion crossing the criminal threshold under Criminal Law Article 201 exposes the responsible persons to fines and imprisonment of up to seven years. Failure to produce contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation can also result in special tax adjustment interest added to the repayment and additional penalties under the tax administration rules.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividend distributions made by the Chinese WFOE to a non-resident enterprise shareholder; treaty relief can reduce this to 5% or 10% depending on the treaty and whether the beneficial owner holds at least 25% of the capital, with many bilateral DTA protocols.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The WFOE as withholding agent must file the non-resident enterprise withholding income tax return in the e-tax system and may apply the reduced DTA rate only if the non-resident beneficial owner submits a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its treaty country, together with a written beneficial-ownership declaration, board resolutions, shareholding register proving the required holding period and percentage, and evidence that the recipient is not a conduit or back-to-back arrangement. The Chinese withholding agent must perform due diligence to confirm the recipient's entitlement, retain the DTA application file, and include the payment in the related-party reporting schedules if the shareholder is a related party. If the WFOE cannot substantiate the application, it must withhold at 10% and the non-resident may claim a refund through the treaty-application procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident income tax of 10% applies to outbound interest and royalties paid to non-resident enterprises without a Chinese establishment; treaty rates generally range from 5% to 10% for royalties and 7% to 10% for interest, subject to beneficial ownership and principal-purpose test. Royalties for intellectual property licensed to the Chinese B2B platform are sourced in China and are subject to withholding on the gross payment unless the recipient is the true beneficial owner. Interest on excessive related-party debt may be denied as a deduction under thin capitalization and may be recharacterized as a distribution, triggering dividend WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under PRC SAT Public Notice 2016 No. 42, a Local File is mandatory if any one of the following related-party transaction thresholds is exceeded in a tax year: tangible asset transfers over RMB 200 million; intangible asset transfers over RMB 100 million; financial-asset transfers over RMB 100 million; related-party financing interest over RMB 10 million; or related-party service transactions over RMB 40 million. A Master File is generally required where the multinational group had consolidated revenue of at least RMB 5 billion in the prior tax year and the Chinese entity is engaged in related-party transactions; Country-by-Country reports may separately be triggered by group revenue thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not operate a formal Economic Substance Regulation filing system in the Gulf-Council style, but economic substance is enforced through the Enterprise Income Tax Law general anti-avoidance rule under Article 47, the reasonable commercial purpose doctrine, and special tax adjustment rules. For the B2B marketplace WFOE, core income-generating activities must be performed in China, including seller onboarding and due diligence, contract negotiation, platform technology and algorithm control, price and promotion decisions, risk assumption, customer and seller support, payment settlement, and logistics quality control. If these functions are merely booked offshore or performed by shell entities, the Chinese tax authority may reattribute profit to the WFOE, deny intercompany deductions, and reject the non-resident shareholder's treaty benefits under the principal-purpose test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Fraud and Artificial Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE makes excessive deductible payments for royalty, management, marketing, and technical service fees to a foreign parent or offshore platform entity without performing a functional analysis, without evidence of actual services, and without contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation, deliberately eroding the Chinese taxable base to near zero.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 41 and 44 authorize the tax bureau to make an arm's-length recharacterization and transfer-pricing adjustment, with interest calculated at the prevailing benchmark rate plus up to five additional percentage points; failure to file or maintain TP documentation is separately punishable under Tax Collection Administration Law Article 62 (RMB 2,000-10,000) and Article 64 (50%-5x of the underpaid tax where false accounting causes underassessment).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced under PRC Company Law Article 20 where a director or controlling shareholder abuses the limited liability structure to evade tax; the responsible director and actual controller become jointly and severally liable for the tax loss. If the conduct is intentional and concealing, Criminal Law Article 201 imposes fines and imprisonment of up to seven years, and the legal representative is subjected to a departure ban, asset freezing, and inclusion in the State Taxation Administration's major tax violation blacklist.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Resident Withholding Tax Evasion on Outbound Profit Remittances
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE declares and remits dividends, interest, or royalties to its non-resident parent or related affiliate without withholding the statutory 10% non-resident income tax, or without filing the treaty relief application and retaining the beneficiary's Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial-ownership evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Collection Administration Law Article 69 requires the withholding agent to remit the tax that should have been withheld and imposes a fine of 50% to three times the amount not withheld; if the underpayment also results from a false return, Article 63 applies with a fine of 50% to five times the underpaid tax. Repeated refusal to pay may trigger enforcement against the company's bank accounts and a blacklisting order.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve dividend declarations without arranging WHT become personally implicated; the legal representative may be blocked from leaving China under Tax Collection Administration Law Article 44 until the full tax, surcharge, and penalties are paid. Willful concealment is treated as criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201, exposing the responsible officer to personal fines, imprisonment of up to seven years, asset restitution, and police/immigration control.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Entity and Lack of Economic Substance with False Preferential Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is maintained as a nominal B2B marketplace store with no real employees, office, platform decisions, or risk management in China; it artificially books the platform revenue while claiming a preferential 15% high-tech rate, small low-profit relief, or treaty-reduced WHT, and uses circular loans or fee arrangements with offshore shell companies only to siphon profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 47 (general anti-avoidance rule) and Article 48 permit the tax authority to recharacterize the arrangement, recompute taxable income, deny the preferential rate, and impose benchmark-based interest plus an additional adjustment of five percentage points; a false claim of a tax preference is a fraudulent reduction of tax liability under Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63, attracting a fine of 50% to five times the underpaid tax plus daily late surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The courts and tax authorities may pierce the corporate veil and treat the WFOE as the alter ego of the foreign parent if it is used purely for tax evasion; shareholders, directors, and actual controllers are jointly liable for the unpaid tax and penalties. Criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 201 applies where false registration, false books, and fraudulent treaty abuse are proven, with imprisonment of up to seven years, fines, confiscation of tax evasion gains, blacklisting, and exit restrictions.
